name: Piper J-3 Cub
summary: Iconic yellow tandem two-seat light trainer of the late 1930s–40s that trained a generation of WWII pilots; many still fly.

wings: Rectangular constant-chord wing with rounded tips, no flaps
engines: Small flat-four with cylinder heads sticking out of each side of the cowl
fuselage: Tailwheel with bungee-sprung V-strut main gear
Usually painted yellow with a black lightning-bolt stripe

tellTales: Engine cylinder heads poking out of each side of the nose
Bright yellow paint with a black lightning-bolt flash along the fuselage
Tiny V-strut high-wing taildragger with tandem seats

confusedWith.howToTell: The Super Cub has a fully enclosed cowl, flaps and often big tires; the J-3 shows exposed cylinder heads and has no flaps.
The Champ has a deeper, rounder forward fuselage with more glazing; the J-3 is slimmer and boxier with exposed cylinders.
The Citabria has a squared-off tail, squared wingtips and spring-steel gear legs; the J-3 has a rounded tail and V-strut gear.
The L-4/J-3 Cub is a tiny narrow-fuselage airplane with a squared tail; the larger L-5 has a long glazed cabin and a six-cylinder cowl.
The J-3 seats two in tandem under a narrow roof; the Taylorcraft seats two side by side in a wider cabin.
The J-3 seats two in tandem in a narrow fuselage; the Chief seats two side by side in a deep, round-sided cabin.
